title: 2017 AMC 12A Problem 1
statement: Pablo buys popsicles for his friends. The store sells single popsicles for \(\$1\) each, \(3\)-popsicle boxes for \(\$2,\) and \(5\)-popsicle boxes for \(\$3.\) What is the greatest number of popsicles that Pablo can buy with \(\$8?\)

solutions.text:
The cheapest popsicles come from the \(5\)-popsicle box, at \(\dfrac{\$3}{5}=\$0.60\) each. Even at that rate, \(14\) popsicles would cost \(14\cdot\$0.60=\$8.40,\) more than \(\$8.\)

So Pablo can buy at most \(13,\) and he achieves this with two \(5\)-boxes for \(\$6\) and one \(3\)-box for \(\$2,\) giving \(2\cdot5+3=13\) popsicles.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The best value is the \(5\)-popsicle box, at \(\$3\) for \(5\)
Spend \(\$6\) on two \(5\)-boxes, then use the remaining \(\$2\) on a \(3\)-box
